Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 732 PM EDT Tue Oct 13 2026

- Some scattered showers tonight into Wednesday morning with a few 
rumbles of thunder, mainly south of M-59.

- More seasonable and drier during the day Wednesday, followed by 
additional rainfall Thursday afternoon into Thursday night.

- A strong cold front delivers gusty winds and much chillier 
conditions Friday, with a few showers in spots.

- Turing drier through the weekend with slightly warmer readings by 
Sunday.

&&

.AVIATION...

A dry cold front continues progressing across Metro Detroit this 
evening, causing wind direction to veer to NNW over the next few 
hours. Loss of daytime heating has already caused gusts to subside 
and will allow southward expansion of lower stratus across the area 
tonight. Highest confidence in MVFR ceilings is at KMBS and KFNT. A 
disturbance aloft brings scattered showers across the area after 
midnight, with an isolated thunderstorm possible mainly south of I-
94. Light wind early Wednesday veers N and NE by Wednesday evening 
as high pressure builds into the northern Great Lakes. Inbound dry 
air favors scattering of lower ceilings during the afternoon, with 
potential for Lake Huron stratus to then move inland Wednesday night.

D21/DTW Convection...An isolated thunderstorm remains possible 
between 08Z and 11Z within scattered coverage of showers, but 
confidence remains too low to include in the TAF at this time.

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* Low for thunderstorms tonight.
